extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media organisations and journalism regulators
extracted.subtask_description: A global set of ethical duties and rights for journalists governing accuracy, independence, methods of information-gathering, privacy, conflicts of interest, and professional conduct, meant to guide reporting and editorial practice across all media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble: public right to information and journalist responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of everyone to have access to information and ideas, reiterated in Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, underpins the journalist's mission. The journalist's responsibility towards the public takes precedence over any other responsibility, in particular towards their employers and the public authorities. Journalism is a profession, which requires time, resources and the means to practise – all of which are essential to its independence. This international declaration specifies the guidelines of conduct for journalists in the research, editing, transmission, dissemination and commentary of news and information, and in the description of events, in any media whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the primacy of public interest, independence of journalism, and applicability across all media and stages of news production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for the facts and the public's right to truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the facts and for the right of the public to truth is the first duty of the journalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend freedom in collection/publication and distinguish fact from comment
rubrics_metrics.description: In pursuance of this duty, the journalist shall at all times defend the principles of freedom in the honest collection and publication of news, and of the right of fair comment and criticism. He/she will make sure to clearly distinguish factual information from commentary and criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires protecting freedom to collect and publish information and actively separating reporting (facts) from opinion and criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report only on facts of known origin; do not suppress or falsify information
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist shall report only in accordance with facts of which he/ she knows the origin. The journalist shall not suppress essential information or falsify any document. He/she will be careful to reproduce faithfully statements and other material that non-public persons publish in social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes faithful reproduction of social media material from non-public persons and forbids suppression of essential information or document falsification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fair methods to obtain information; disclose journalist status; limit covert methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist shall use only fair methods to obtain information, images, documents and data and he/she will always report his/her status as a journalist and will refrain from using hidden recordings of images and sounds, except where it is impossible for him/her to collect information that is overwhelmingly in the public interest. He/she will demand free access to all sources of information and the right to freely investigate all facts of public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits covert methods only in exceptional cases of overwhelming public interest; requires claiming journalist status and demanding access to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification over immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of urgency or immediacy in the dissemination of information shall not take precedence over the verification of facts, sources and/or the offer of a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise fact-checking and offering subjects a chance to reply before rushing to publish for speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, explicit, complete and transparent correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist shall do the utmost to rectify any errors or published information which is found to be inaccurate in a timely, explicit, complete and transparent manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections must be prompt and clear, addressing inaccuracies fully and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional secrecy of confidential sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist shall observe professional secrecy regarding the source of information obtained in confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidential sources unless release is required by overriding lawful process or circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for privacy, dignity, and vulnerable interviewees; inform about publication intent
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist will respect privacy. He/she shall respect the dignity of the persons named and/or represented and inform the interviewee whether the conversation and other material is intended for publication. He/she shall show particular consideration to inexperienced and vulnerable interviewees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires informing interviewees when material is for publication and exercising extra care with vulnerable individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contributing to hatred or prejudice; prevent discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists shall ensure that the dissemination of information or opinion does not contribute to hatred or prejudice and shall do their utmost to avoid facilitating the spread of discrimination on grounds such as geographical, social or ethnic origin, race, gender, sexual orientation, language, religion, disability, political and other opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to guard against content that fuels discrimination or hatred across numerous protected characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious professional misconduct defined
rubrics_metrics.description:
The journalist will consider serious professional misconduct to be
plagiarism
distortion of facts
slander, libel, defamation, unfounded accusations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists concrete examples of conduct that constitute grave ethical breaches: plagiarism, factual distortion, and unjustified defamatory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not act as auxiliary to police or security services
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist shall refrain from acting as an auxiliary of the police or other security services. He/she will only be required to provide information already published in a media outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves editorial independence from law enforcement; only publicly-published information may be demanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solidarity with colleagues while preserving freedom to investigate and criticise
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist will show solidarity with his/her colleagues, without renouncing his/her freedom of investigation, duty to inform, and right to engage in criticism, commentary, satire and editorial choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages mutual support among journalists but not at the expense of independent reporting or critical expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest and undue personal gain
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist shall not use the freedom of the press to serve any other interest and shall refrain from receiving any unfair advantage or personal gain because of the dissemination or non-dissemination of information. He/she will avoid - or put an end to - any situation that could lead him/her to a conflict of interest in the exercise of his/her profession. He/she will avoid any confusion between his activity and that of advertising or propaganda. He/she will refrain from any form of insider trading and market manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits using press position for personal benefit, necessitates separation from advertising/propaganda, and forbids insider trading tied to journalistic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain independence; respect agreed confidentiality arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalist will not undertake any activity or engagement likely to put his/her independence in danger. He/she will, however, respect the methods of collection/dissemination of information that he / she has freely accepted, such as "off the record", anonymity, or embargo, provided that these commitments are clear and unquestionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance between avoiding compromising engagements and honouring clear confidentiality or embargo agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of conscience and protection from coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists worthy of the name shall deem it their duty to observe faithfully the principles stated above. They may not be compelled to perform a professional act or to express an opinion that is contrary to his/her professional conviction or conscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects journalists from being forced to act or speak against their ethical convictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of independent self-regulatory bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the general law of each country the journalist shall recognize in matters of professional honour, the jurisdiction of independent self-regulatory bodies open to the public, to the exclusion of every kind of interference by governments or others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports self-regulation and public-facing complaints/disciplinary mechanisms free from government interference, in accordance with national law.
